sources.title: Master Direction – KYC (Amendment) Direction, 2026
sources.summary: Annual re-KYC for high-risk customers, beneficial ownership threshold cut to 10%, mandatory PAN-Aadhaar verification, CRILC reporting of KYC exceptions, eight-year retention and board-level governance.

sources.title: Digital Lending Directions, 2025 – Amendment 2026
sources.summary: Default loss guarantee cap raised to 10%, vernacular key fact statement with explicit acknowledgement, cooling-off period extended to seven days and CIC reporting of lending service providers.

sources.title: Cyber Security and Cyber Resilience Framework – Amendment 2026
sources.summary: 24x7 SOC monitoring with 180-day log retention, annual third-party cyber assessments and six-hour incident reporting to SEBI.

assets.name: KYC & Customer Due Diligence Policy
assets.state: Policy prescribes biennial re-KYC for high-risk customers and a 25% beneficial ownership threshold.
assets.gap: Sections 4.1, 6.3 and Annexure B carry the superseded thresholds.

assets.name: AML / CFT Policy
assets.state: Covers STR filing and customer risk rating; there is no CRILC exception reporting workflow.
assets.gap: No section on KYC exception reporting or Principal Officer sign-off.

assets.name: Data Privacy & Retention Policy
assets.state: Retention schedule sets five years for KYC records and does not cover consent artefacts.
assets.gap: Retention period and consent audit-trail clauses are outdated.

assets.name: Outsourcing & Third-Party Risk Policy
assets.state: Annual vendor reviews exist; there is no board approval step for outsourcing a regulated function.
assets.gap: Board approval and materiality classification are missing.

assets.name: Board Governance Charter
assets.state: Board reviews the KYC policy annually and the Audit Committee meets half-yearly.
assets.gap: Review cadence is below the amended requirement.

assets.name: Digital Lending Policy
assets.state: Permits a 5% default loss guarantee cap and a three-day cooling-off period.
assets.gap: DLG cap and cooling-off period are below the amended requirement.

assets.name: Cyber Security Policy
assets.state: SOC coverage is business hours only; logs are retained for 90 days.
assets.gap: Monitoring window and log retention fall short.

assets.name: Retail Customer Onboarding
assets.state: Capture, CKYC check and manual BO declaration; PAN-Aadhaar linkage is checked after account opening.
assets.gap: Verification is post-facto and the BO cut-off is 25%.

assets.name: Periodic KYC Review
assets.state: Review dates are generated by a monthly batch using a 24-month high-risk cycle.
assets.gap: Batch cycle and reminders need re-parameterisation.

assets.name: High-Risk Customer Review
assets.state: EDD checklist covers source of funds; there is no trigger-based risk re-rating between reviews.
assets.gap: No event-driven review trigger.

assets.name: Beneficial Ownership Determination
assets.state: Ops traces shareholding to 25% using MCA filings and a manual declaration.
assets.gap: Manual tracing and annual refresh are not defined.

assets.name: Regulatory Reporting – CRILC
assets.state: Monthly CRILC upload covers large credit exposures only; there is no KYC exception feed.
assets.gap: No exception data, no seven-day SLA.

assets.name: Records Management
assets.state: Retention schedule is applied by record class; KYC records are destroyed after five years.
assets.gap: Retention and retrieval SLAs are short of the amendment.

assets.name: Account Aggregator Consent Flow
assets.state: Consent is journey-level, is not purpose-bound and cannot be revoked in-app.
assets.gap: Consent model does not meet purpose limitation or revocation.

assets.name: Video KYC (V-CIP)
assets.state: Agent-led video call; recording stored for five years; no liveness or geo-tag check.
assets.gap: Liveness, geo-tagging and retention are non-compliant.

assets.name: Key Fact Statement Delivery
assets.state: KFS is generated in English only and acknowledged through a click-through in the app.
assets.gap: No vernacular KFS and acknowledgement is not an explicit action.

assets.name: Cooling-Off and Exit
assets.state: Three-day cooling-off window; exit requests are handled through the grievance desk.
assets.gap: Window is shorter than the amended requirement.

assets.name: Vendor Onboarding & Review
assets.state: Vendors are risk-rated annually; cyber assessment is a self-attestation questionnaire.
assets.gap: No independent cyber assessment before onboarding.

assets.name: Cyber Incident Response
assets.state: Incidents are reported to the regulator within 24 hours after internal triage.
assets.gap: Reporting SLA and RCA timeline are longer than permitted.

assets.name: Grievance Redressal
assets.state: Complaints are logged in CRM; there is no linkage to regulatory reporting.
assets.gap: No regulatory tagging of complaints.

assets.name: CIF / Core Banking System
assets.state: Customer master stores one BO percentage field hard-coded at 25 and derives the review date from the risk tier.
assets.gap: Schema and batch logic encode the old thresholds.

assets.name: Digital Onboarding Portal
assets.state: Journey calls CKYC and PAN validation APIs; Aadhaar linkage status is not checked.
assets.gap: No PAN-Aadhaar linkage API call at journey start.

assets.name: CKYC Registry Adapter
assets.state: Pushes records to CERSAI CKYC and retries failed uploads for 24 hours.
assets.gap: No change feed for re-KYC updates.

assets.name: AML Screening Engine
assets.state: Screens sanctions and PEP lists at onboarding and nightly; risk score is static.
assets.gap: Risk score is not recalculated on trigger events.

assets.name: CRILC Reporting Module
assets.state: Generates the monthly large-credit file; there is no exception or KYC data feed.
assets.gap: No KYC exception schema or seven-day scheduler.

assets.name: Document Management System
assets.state: Retention rules are configured per document class; purge job runs at five years.
assets.gap: Retention rule and retrieval index need updating.

assets.name: V-CIP Module
assets.state: Records video to object storage; no liveness SDK and no geo-tag capture.
assets.gap: Liveness and geo-tagging must be added to the capture flow.

assets.name: Consent & Preference Hub
assets.state: Stores consent flags per product; revocation requires a support ticket.
assets.gap: No purpose-bound consent artefact or immutable trail.

assets.name: Workflow & Notification Engine
assets.state: Sends email and SMS from static templates; no regulatory task routing.
assets.gap: No regulatory task queue or escalation.

assets.name: Loan Management System
assets.state: Calculates DLG exposure at 5% and enforces a three-day cooling-off flag.
assets.gap: Hard-coded DLG cap and cooling-off window.

assets.name: KFS Generator
assets.state: Renders an English KFS PDF from the loan schedule; acknowledgement is a click event.
assets.gap: Single-language template and weak acknowledgement.

assets.name: SOC / SIEM
assets.state: Monitors production systems during business hours; hot storage retained for 90 days.
assets.gap: Coverage window and retention are short of the framework.

assets.name: Vendor Risk Platform
assets.state: Tracks vendor contracts and annual review dates; cyber questionnaire is manual.
assets.gap: No cyber scoring or pre-onboarding gate.

assets.name: CRM & Service Desk
assets.state: Ticketing for complaints and service requests; no regulatory tagging.
assets.gap: No regulatory taxonomy on cases.

assets.name: Customer Risk Rating (CDD-01)
assets.state: Risk rating is assigned at onboarding and refreshed annually.
assets.gap: Trigger-based re-rating is not evidenced.

assets.name: Beneficial Ownership Check (CDD-04)
assets.state: Four-eyes check on the BO declaration; threshold documented as 25%.
assets.gap: Control description and test script use the old threshold.

assets.name: Periodic Review Scheduler (KYC-07)
assets.state: Batch scheduler produces review tasks from the CIF review date.
assets.gap: Scheduler parameters and exception reporting are manual.

assets.name: Regulatory Reporting Reconciliation (RPT-03)
assets.state: Monthly reconciliation of CRILC and other regulatory extracts.
assets.gap: No reconciliation for KYC exceptions.

assets.name: Retention Schedule (REC-02)
assets.state: Record-class retention matrix approved by the Board.
assets.gap: Matrix reflects five-year retention.

assets.name: KFS Delivery Check (DL-01)
assets.state: Sampling check that KFS was delivered before disbursal.
assets.gap: Sample does not verify language or explicit acknowledgement.

assets.name: Consent Audit (PRV-05)
assets.state: Quarterly sample audit of consent artefacts.
assets.gap: Audit does not test purpose limitation or revocation.

clauses.heading: Insertion of new Section 9A — key fact statement
clauses.subject: key fact statement
clauses.text:
Insertion of new Section 9A — key fact statement
After Section 9 of the Directions, the following section shall be inserted, namely:
9A. Key fact statement
(1) Every Regulated Entity shall provide a key fact statement to the borrower in English and in the language of the State where the borrower resides.
(2) The key fact statement shall include the annual percentage rate, the total cost of credit, the recovery agent details and the grievance redressal mechanism.
(3) The borrower shall acknowledge receipt of the key fact statement through an explicit action, and the acknowledgement shall be retained for eight years.

Insertion of new Section 15A — reporting of lending service providers
After Section 15 of the Directions, the following section shall be inserted, namely:
15A. Reporting of lending service providers
(1) Every Regulated Entity shall report the onboarding, termination and material change in the ownership of a lending service provider to the Credit Information Companies within fifteen calendar days.
(2) The Regulated Entity shall conduct an annual information security audit of every lending service provider and shall report the findings to the Board.

clauses.text:
Insertion of new Clause 6A — third party risk
Every regulated entity shall conduct a cyber security assessment of every third party service provider before onboarding and at least once every twelve months thereafter.
Where the assessment identifies a material gap, the regulated entity shall not share customer data with the service provider until the gap is remediated.

clauses.heading: Amendment to Section 16 — periodic updation of KYC
clauses.subject: periodic updation of KYC
clauses.text:
Amendment to Section 16 — periodic updation of KYC
In the Master Direction, for Section 16, the following section shall be substituted, namely:
16. Periodic updation of KYC
(1) Every Regulated Entity shall carry out periodic updation of KYC records at the following intervals:
(a) high-risk customers — at least once every twelve months;
(b) medium-risk customers — at least once every twenty-four months;
(c) low-risk customers — at least once every thirty-six months.
(2) The risk categorisation of every customer shall be reviewed on the occurrence of a trigger event and in any case not less than once every six months.
(3) Where a customer fails to submit the required documents within thirty days of a request, the Regulated Entity shall suspend operations in the account until the records are updated.

clauses.heading: Amendment to Section 17 — beneficial ownership
clauses.subject: beneficial ownership
clauses.text:
Amendment to Section 17 — beneficial ownership
In the Master Direction, for sub-section (3) of Section 17, the following shall be substituted, namely:
17(3) For the purposes of this Direction, beneficial owner means an individual who ultimately owns or controls a customer and includes:
(a) in the case of a company, the natural person who owns or controls more than ten per cent of the shares or voting rights;
(b) in the case of a partnership firm, the natural person who owns or controls more than ten per cent of the capital or profits;
(c) in the case of a trust, the author, the trustee and the beneficiary, where the trust holds more than ten per cent of the shares or capital.
The Regulated Entity shall identify and verify every beneficial owner before onboarding and shall refresh the ownership determination at least once every twelve months.

clauses.heading: Insertion of new Section 18A — verification of PAN and Aadhaar
clauses.subject: verification of PAN and Aadhaar
clauses.text:
Insertion of new Section 18A — verification of PAN and Aadhaar
After Section 18 of the Master Direction, the following section shall be inserted, namely:
18A. Verification of PAN and Aadhaar
(1) Every Regulated Entity shall, at the time of onboarding and before every high-value transaction exceeding rupees ten lakh, verify that the Permanent Account Number of the customer is active and linked with Aadhaar.
(2) Where the verification fails, the Regulated Entity shall not commence or continue the relationship and shall record the failure in the exception register within twenty-four hours.
(3) The exception register shall be reviewed by the Principal Officer every month.

Insertion of new Section 22A — reporting of KYC exceptions

(2) The report shall be approved by the Principal Officer and shall be retained for a period of eight years.
(3) The Board shall be informed of the number and nature of exceptions every quarter.

clauses.heading: Insertion of new Section 38A — consent based data sharing
clauses.subject: consent based data sharing
clauses.text:
Insertion of new Section 38A — consent based data sharing
After Section 38 of the Master Direction, the following section shall be inserted, namely:
38A. Consent based data sharing
(1) Every Regulated Entity shall obtain explicit, purpose-bound and revocable consent from the customer before sharing KYC data with any third party, including an account aggregator.
(2) The Regulated Entity shall maintain an immutable audit trail of every consent, including the purpose, the recipient and the time of revocation, and shall produce it within forty-eight hours of a request.
(3) Consent shall not be obtained as a condition for availing any basic banking service.
